short_original_summary: Use the four number operations and brackets.
Use primes, factors and multiples including HCF/LCM.
Use indices, powers and roots.
Manipulate simple surds and preserve exact answers.
Rationalise denominators.
Recognise natural, integer, rational and irrational sets.
Calculate using standard measures and supplied currency rates.
Use fractions, decimals, ratios, proportion and percentages.
Round to a given degree of accuracy.
Solve problems using measurement bounds.
Use standard form in calculations and contexts.
Define sets and identify their distinct members.
Use set language in abstract and practical situations.
Form unions and intersections, including rule-defined sets.
Count elements using set-size notation.
Find complements within a stated universe.
Recognise and use subset relationships.
Identify the universal and empty sets.
Use Venn diagrams for simple logical problems.
Represent set relationships with symbols.
Simplify algebraic expressions using operations and integer or fractional index rules.
Construct, interpret, substitute into and rearrange formulae.
Factorise simple algebraic expressions.
Apply the factor theorem to polynomials, including cubics and general linear factors.
Divide a cubic polynomial by a linear factor.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide simple algebraic fractions with numerical, linear or quadratic denominators.
Solve linear, quadratic and cubic equations in one unknown, including algebraic/graphical quadratic methods and problems leading to equations.
Solve simultaneous linear equations in two unknowns, including graphical solutions.
Solve simultaneous equations where one equation is linear and the other quadratic.
Solve linear inequalities and represent their solutions on number lines and in two-dimensional space, including simultaneous regions.
Solve quadratic inequalities in one unknown and represent the solution set on a number line.
Recognise and continue sequences with common differences and common integer patterns.
Prove that two triangles are similar, giving geometric reasons and consistent correspondence.
Use cyclic-quadrilateral properties, including opposite interior and adjacent exterior angle reasoning.
Direct and inverse variation only in the explicitly listed x, x², x³, √x and reciprocal forms; historical Q19 inverse cube-root applicability remains unresolved.
Angle properties of parallel lines, triangles and polygons, including regular polygons, straight-line and full-turn angles.
Determine mean, median and mode for discrete data.
Relate a straight-line equation y = mx + c to its gradient and y-axis intercept (0,c).
Add and multiply matrices; row-by-column multiplication of order at most 3 × 3.
Multiply a matrix by a scalar.
Use Pythagoras in two and three dimensions, including constructed or given altitudes; angle-bisector theorems excluded.
Calculate areas of rectangles, parallelograms, trapezia, triangles and circles, including shapes decomposed into these.
Use SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS conditions to prove two triangles congruent.
Use sine, cosine and tangent for angles up to 180°, measured in degrees and decimals of degrees.
Use angles of elevation and depression in degrees and decimals of degrees.
Determine determinants and inverses of non-singular 2×2 matrices; knowledge of singular matrices is not required.
Use chord, angle and tangent properties of circles, including internal and external intersecting chords and the alternate segment theorem.
Estimate a mean from grouped frequencies; separate weighted and moving mean questions will not be set.
Determine a modal class and the class containing the median in grouped data.
Use basic probability language, scales, sample spaces, relative frequency, probabilities and complements.
Relate length scale factors to area and volume factors for similar figures.
Calculate arc lengths and sector areas in degrees; radians excluded.
Use parallel vectors, unit vectors and position vectors in two dimensions.
Find sums and differences of vectors.
Multiply a vector by a scalar.
Apply vectors to simple geometry, including collinearity, parallel lines and concurrency.
Differentiate integer powers of x using dy/dx notation.
Determine gradients, rates of change, stationary points, maxima, minima and turning points with graph interpretation.
Represent numerical data with bar charts, pie charts and histograms; cumulative frequency graphs excluded.
Add probabilities of mutually exclusive events.
Multiply probabilities of independent events.
Determine probabilities of two or more independent events using tree diagrams.
Use simple conditional probability for combined events.
Find very simple conditional probability; formal conditional notation is not used.
Understand and calculate expected frequency.
The idea of a function of a variable.
Functions as mappings or correspondences between elements of two sets.
Use f(x) and mapping-arrow functional notation.
Domain and range, including excluded inputs; continuity questions excluded.
Composite functions, with fg meaning apply g then f.
Find inverse functions.
Draw and interpret numerical cubic/quadratic/linear/constant/reciprocal combinations with at least three of six coefficients zero; solve by graph intersections.
Estimate gradients by a drawn tangent and an appropriate right-angled gradient triangle.
Apply functions to linear kinematics and simple practical problems; interpret distance/speed-time graphs and displacement/velocity/acceleration relationships.
Distinguish scalar and vector quantities in two dimensions.
Understand and use directed and column vector notation.
Represent a vector with a directed line segment.
Calculate and interpret the modulus or magnitude of a two-dimensional vector.
Find the resultant of two or more vectors.
